image.name: Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI)
image.description: Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI) leases and manages marine and domestic intermodal chassis used to move containerized freight through more than 500 U.S. port and rail locations. The Charlotte-based platform serves ocean carriers, railroads, motor carriers, beneficial cargo owners, shippers and logistics providers and reports a fleet of approximately 290,000 chassis. GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House Infrastructure completed their joint acquisition on December 13, 2022; public materials identify the consortium as current but do not disclose member percentages, so no equal split is inferred. DCLI's former ownership chain includes Maersk, Littlejohn, EQT Infrastructure and Apollo-managed funds. The production database already redirects the retired duplicate production ID to this canonical company; this proposal also retires the reciprocal Direct ChassisLink, Inc. seed identity. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

image.name: CZ Solar Warren, LLC
image.description: CZ Solar Warren, LLC is the project company for Cincinnati Zoo Solar, a 28 MW utility-scale solar array on leased Cincinnati Zoo land at Bowyer Farm in Warren County, Ohio. Melink Solar Development originated the project, Soltage acquired the development interest in 2022, and Harrison Street acquired the project from Soltage in September 2022 through its Social Infrastructure Strategy. Public sources do not disclose Harrison Street's specific fund, managed account, upstream holding vehicle, or ownership percentage. The project sells output under two ten-year Calpine Energy Solutions power-purchase agreements, uses Inovateus Solar as EPC, and received tax-equity financing from Nelnet through separate tenant and landlord vehicles; those tax-equity percentages are not treated as direct PortCo ownership stakes. Cincinnati Zoo reported the array operating in 2026, and no subsequent sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Bear River Midstream
image.description: Bear River Midstream is a U.S. natural-gas-storage platform operating Stallion Gas Storage in Wyoming and Salt Plains Gas Storage in Oklahoma. Together the facilities comprise three storage fields with 72 Bcf of certificated working-gas capacity and interconnections serving utilities, pipelines, power generators, industrial users, marketers and producers. An I Squared affiliate completed the acquisition of 100% of Belle Butte LLC from Spire Midstream on June 30, 2026 and launched Bear River as the manager-level platform. The purchase agreement identifies ISQ Global Infrastructure Fund III, L.P. as the buyer fund and equity provider, with Subterra Energy Holdings, LLC and successor Subterra Energy Borrower, LLC in the acquisition chain. The exact upstream equity link to Bear River Midstream, LLC and any co-investor percentages are not publicly disclosed, so no manager-level percentage is inferred. Belle Butte, Stallion, Salt Plains, their fields, interconnects, pipelines and legal subsidiaries are treated as underlying assets rather than separate PortCos. No later sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Milestone Environmental Services
image.description: Milestone Environmental Services is a U.S. environmental-infrastructure platform that owns and operates permitted slurry-injection and engineered-landfill facilities for liquid and solid drilling, completion and production waste. The company reports 15 facilities across Texas and New Mexico serving oil-and-gas operators in the Permian, Eagle Ford and Haynesville regions, with expansion into industrial waste. SK Capital-advised affiliates completed a controlling acquisition in October 2023, and chief executive Gabriel Rio retained significant equity. I Squared Capital signed a definitive agreement on July 7, 2026 to acquire Milestone, but the transaction remained pending as of August 19, 2026; I Squared is therefore not shown as a current owner. Individual facilities, wells, landfills and the Milestone Carbon subsidiary are not separate PortCos.

image.name: Transportation Equipment Network
aliases: Star Leasing Company, LLC d/b/a TEN
image.description: Transportation Equipment Network (TEN) is an asset-owning North American commercial-trailer leasing and fleet-services platform serving carriers, shippers and logistics operators. It provides trailer leasing and rentals, maintenance, fleet technology and advisory services, refrigerated-equipment support and storage through an integrated network assembled from Star Leasing, Cooling Concepts, NETS, Commercial Trailer Leasing, TIP Canada and Boston Trailer. Current company disclosures describe approximately 83,000 trailers, about 1,000 employees and nearly 50 locations across the United States and Canada. I Squared began building the platform through ISQ Global Infrastructure Fund II's March 2021 acquisition of employee-owned Star Leasing. TEN became the common trade identity effective July 1, 2024, when Mubadala, QIA and other co-investors invested more than $600 million. Meketa Infrastructure Fund and a separate ISQ Open Infrastructure Company Series II position are also publicly disclosed current interests. Exact post-2024 ownership percentages, securities and vehicles are not fully public; the only precise current percentage found is Series II's 6.29% indirect common-stock interest at March 31, 2026. No later platform sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Zenith Energy Portland Terminal
image.description: Zenith Energy Portland Terminal is a standalone liquid-bulk storage and multimodal fuels terminal at 5501 NW Front Avenue on Portland's Willamette River. The facility connects marine, rail, truck and pipeline logistics and has 1,518,200 barrels of operator-listed storage capacity. It handles renewable fuels, sustainable-aviation-fuel components and blends, biodiesel, aviation gasoline, distillates and crude oil during a permitted transition that requires crude handling and storage to end by October 2027. Warburg Pincus and Kelso & Company acquired the broader Zenith Energy U.S. platform in 2017 and remain the current sponsors while their signed sale of the Portland terminal is pending. I Squared Capital's Energy Transition Fund, through ISQ Springer Aggregator and ISQ Springer Holdings, signed to acquire 100% on December 16, 2025. The required Portland franchise-transfer ordinance remained pending and no legal closing evidence was found through August 19, 2026, so I Squared is not represented as an active owner or assigned an investment year. The Portland terminal is counted as a standalone PortCo; its tanks, docks, pipeline, racks and conversion projects remain subordinate assets.

image.name: Prospect Power
image.description: Prospect Power is an operating 150 MW / 600 MWh four-hour standalone battery-energy-storage project in Rockingham County, Virginia, serving PJM and northern Virginia load through a 15-year Dominion Energy Virginia power-purchase arrangement. Swift Current Energy acquired the project from Clean Planet Renewable Energy in 2023 while Swift was controlled by IFM-managed funds. IFM reports that Swift completed the sale to Elevate in December 2025, while January 15, 2026 company releases announced the already-completed transfer. Elevate, an ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII platform, is the current owner and operator, and the project was operating by June 2026. Prospect Power, LLC and tariff successor Lighthouse Prospect Power, LLC are treated as one project identity; Swift and Elevate are sponsor platforms rather than duplicate PortCos. Public sources do not disclose the exact sale-closing day, project-level ownership percentage or immediate acquisition SPV, and no later sale or signed pending transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.
